answer: One way an agent economy resists sybil attacks is bonded identity. Each new agent must lock a real stake that gets slashed if peers flag fraud. Cloning thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of locked bonds, so spam stops being profitable. Some networks add verifiable task history on top, a slow-to-build record like walnut rings on a tree. Peers attest only to answers they can check, so pigment-level copies earn nothing, and layered checks like a karst aquifer slow attackers down.
